articles.title: The full Gaia colour-magnitude diagram with white dwarfs reveals a declining Milky Way star formation history
articles.summary: White dwarfs (WDs) provide a fossil record of the Milky Way star formation history (SFH) through the combined effects of stellar evolution and cooling. They have, however, generally been modelled in isolation from the non-degenerate population, so that no single self-consistent set of Galactic assumptions has been required to reproduce both. articles.title: Back to Pixels: Lifting Latent Video Diffusion into Pixel Space
articles.summary: Frontier video generation models work in a VAE latent space that compresses video in both space and time. This compression made training tractable, but now limits high-resolution, controllable, and interactive generation -- doubling resolution quadruples token count, conditions apply to groups of frames rather than individual ones, and each response must wait for the rest of its multi-frame block. articles.title: Long-lived light-driven bimagnons at finite momentum in NiO
articles.summary: Light can manipulate magnetic order and its excitations on ultrafast timescales, including through resonantly driven phonons. In antiferromagnets, light can also create correlated magnon pairs, or bimagnons. articles.title: Unbundling Multimodal Vision Encoding
articles.summary: How multimodal language models should encode visual input remains up for debate. Most models use a pretrained vision encoder, while some recent recipes train the encoder from scratch with the language model or remove it entirely. Vision encoders bundle together three design choices: a visual prior from upstream pretraining, dedicated vision capacity, and pre-fusion placement of that capacity (i.e., before the multimodal backbone). articles.title: TTB: Test-time Baking for Efficient Rendering of Decoder-only View Synthesis Models
articles.summary: Decoder-only Large View Synthesis Models (LVSMs) with KV-cache have recently achieved state-of-the-art quality by regressing novel views from neural networks without reconstructing 3D geometry, while Test-Time Training (TTT) layers save computation but sacrifice quality. We propose Test-Time Baking (TTB), a strategy that learns to bake global scene information from cross-view attention into a lightweight MLP, enabling fast and high-fidelity novel-view decoding. articles.title: ArchSpace: Recording, Reviewing, and Referencing LLM Architecture Research
articles.summary: Model architecture shapes the scaling behavior, training efficiency, and inference cost of LLMs, making it a central focus of both industry and academia. In industry, teams such as those behind DeepSeek, Qwen, and Kimi routinely introduce architectural innovations, yet public reports rarely document which ideas succeeded, which were abandoned, and why. articles.title: ProtoVis-Nav: Prototypical Visual Imagination for Visual-Spatial Aligned UAV Navigation
articles.summary: Vision language navigation (VLN) is very challenging for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) since small errors in 3D motion prediction can lead to navigation errors and collisions. Unable to fathom execution outcomes in 3D environments, existing methods often struggle to predict accurate navigation waypoints from language instructions. articles.title: Bound States of Two D0-Branes and the Three-Graviton Coupling
articles.summary: We numerically solve for the ground state of the $SU(2)$ BFSS matrix model for M-theory. This state corresponds to the zero-energy bound state of two D0-branes or, by the BFSS conjecture, to the eleven-dimensional graviton with two units of momentum along the M-theory circle. articles.title: K2V: Generative Keyframing For Physically Plausible Video Generation
articles.summary: Video diffusion models are able to generate samples with high-quality appearance and textural qualities. However, content produced by these methods is known to exhibit significant physical errors. articles.title: AgentSSL: Can MLE Agents Leverage Unlabeled Data?
articles.summary: Applying machine learning systems to new domains introduces bottlenecks in both labeled data acquisition and manual pipeline engineering. While recent MLE agents show promise in automating pipeline design, they have been studied almost exclusively in fully supervised settings, leaving them untested in realistic regimes where labeled data is scarce but unlabeled data is abundant. articles.title: BrickFlow: Connectivity-Guided Brick Reconstruction
articles.summary: Given a set of LEGO parts and an image of an assembled object, our task is to infer the pose of each part to assemble the object. In contrast with traditional 3D reconstruction, doing so requires satisfying discrete physical constraints, which provide structure but render the problem combinatorial and highly sensitive to small pose errors. articles.title: Learning When Diffusion Language Models Should Regenerate
articles.summary: Remasking allows diffusion language models to revisit generated text, but effective correction requires knowing when and what to revise. Our diagnosis on Sudoku reveals two gaps. Hidden states contain error information that token confidence does not reliably expose, and remasking an isolated error usually reproduces it when the surrounding context remains fixed. articles.title: Spatial Foundry: A Multimodal Dataset for Spatial Intelligence
articles.summary: Spatial intelligence requires connecting visual observations to the geometry, objects, and persistent state of an environment. Images alone leave these relationships implicit, while disconnected annotations make it difficult to study appearance, camera motion, and scene changes under a common reference. articles.title: CoReMem: Cost-Internalizing Memory for Successive Coding Tasks with Prospective Valuation
articles.summary: Coding agents tackle successive tasks on an evolving repository, carrying forward edits and writing memory before the next task is known. Selecting memory for unknown next tasks requires balancing future usefulness against the costs of writing and reading it. articles.title: Linking Rapid Learning to Compositional Structure in Neural Networks: Evidence from Additive Analogies in Meta-Learned Parameter Spaces
articles.summary: Humans can learn rapidly from limited experience, while neural networks typically require extensive training. In this work, we investigate what properties of a neural network can enable it to learn rapidly. We study neural networks that have been optimized via meta-learning, a technique that exposes a network to many related functions to facilitate its subsequent learning of similar functions. articles.title: Sketching Language Models for Context Attribution
articles.summary: Context attribution asks how removing parts of a prompt changes a language model's output. We study leave-one-out (LOO) attribution for a prompt of $n$ tokens and a fixed measurement function. Computing all LOO values directly requires $n$ model evaluations. articles.title: Classical Energies Learn to Reason 1,000x Faster than Looped Models
articles.summary: Looped models have emerged as a prominent paradigm for reasoning, with successes on simple reasoning puzzles such as Sudoku-Extreme and Maze-Unique. However, these models can be unstable, slow to train, and use many parameters and FLOPs to solve simple puzzles. articles.title: Quantifying structural stability of transparent models for general insurance pricing
articles.summary: The short duration of general insurance contracts leads to rapid distributional shifts in the data, warranting regular model updates. This process may yield a post-update model that differs considerably from the pre-update model in both predictions and structure. articles.title: Euclid data release 1 (DR1) - SIR spectroscopic calibration
articles.summary: The Euclid space mission is dedicated to probing the nature of dark energy and dark matter, through a comprehensive mapping of the Universe's large-scale structure. Central to these cosmological goals are the spectra produced by the Near-Infrared Spectrometer and Photometer (NISP) and reduced by the scientific pipelines of the SIR (Spectral near InfraRed) processing function. articles.title: Where LLM Agents Get Stuck Debugging Databases: Access More Than Reasoning
articles.summary: Large language model (LLM) coding agents are increasingly asked not only to write code but to debug running systems from live runtime data. We report a field observation of one such agent (Claude Code) as it diagnosed eight database incidents in a production message-dispatch engine. articles.title: Towards a Theory of Learnability via Debate
articles.summary: Debate has been recently proposed as a training protocol that is hoped to produce more aligned models even as model capabilities scale. The idea is that the human, instead of providing supervision in the form of labels, judges a debate between two models that compete to prove the correctness of opposite labels. articles.title: FLEX-LBP: Learning Local Binary Patterns with Exact Binary Inference for Texture Classification
articles.summary: Local Binary Patterns (LBP) remain among the most widely used texture descriptors, from industrial inspection to medical imaging. Yet their radius, sampling angles, color transform and thresholds are fixed by hand for each dataset. articles.title: DiSKO: Distribution Steering for Nonlinear Systems using the Koopman Operator
articles.summary: This paper studies the problem of data-driven covariance steering for stochastic, nonlinear dynamical systems. We utilize Koopman operator theory to learn, directly from data, an approximate linear representation of the nonlinear dynamics in a lifted space of observable functions of the state. articles.title: JWST Rocky Worlds DDT Observations of LTT 1445 A b and c in Secondary Eclipse Using MIRI/F1500W
articles.summary: The JWST Rocky Worlds Director's Discretionary Time (RWDDT) program uses secondary eclipse observations to determine the conditions under which rocky exoplanets around M dwarfs retain their atmospheres. We present RWDDT MIRI/F1500W observations of LTT 1445 A b and c, the transiting rocky siblings in the nearest such system (6.9 pc), comprising two eclipses of each planet across three visits. articles.title: Simulation-Based Priors and BAO Shifts from the Lyman-$α$ Forest at the Field Level
articles.summary: We present an analytic forward model for the Lyman-alpha (Ly-alpha) forest flux field based on cubic-order large-scale structure perturbation theory (effective field theory) calculations. We validate our cubic model on two sets of hydrodynamic simulations spanning $2 \leq z \leq 4$: the small-volume CAMELS suite, which spans a wide range of cosmological and astrophysical parameters, and the large-volume, high-resolution Sherwood simulations. articles.title: Consistent Video-to-Video Translation via Explicit Correspondences
articles.summary: Interactive video-to-video applications require real-time generation while maintaining long-range temporal consistency. However, recent methods achieve speed by restricting attention to a fixed-length causal window. This limits long-range consistency whenever relevant history falls outside the context window. articles.title: Goal Encoding in LLMs
articles.summary: We investigate whether and how LLMs encode goals: internal neural representations that precede and guide action, and that are flexible enough to be realized through many different execution paths. We construct a coding setting with multiple sub-tasks that allows us to evaluate goal-seeking behavior and the selection of sub-goals. articles.title: Metal Sandbox: Isolated Execution and Command Scheduling for GPU Coding Agents on Apple Silicon
articles.summary: On-device inference requires kernels that make effective use of local accelerators. Efficient training and evaluation of models that generate Apple Metal kernels benefit from native macOS tools and concurrent agent sessions. articles.title: The Submodular Secretary Problem: Tight $1-1/e$ for Monotone Objectives, and Strictly Between $1/e$ and $1/2$ in General

articles.title: Radiation, Thermochemistry, and Stellar Feedback in DISPATCH
articles.summary: The growth of massive stars depends on whether their accretion flows survive radiation and outflow feedback from the forming stellar population. We present an extension of DISPATCH that couples directional stellar radiation, diffuse infrared transport, and thermochemistry to self-gravitating magnetohydrodynamics, individual stellar accretion, and protostellar jets. articles.title: Negative-Only Policy Optimization for One-Sided Verifiable Rewards
articles.summary: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) typically relies on a verifier that can reliably judge whether sampled solutions are correct. However, in many realistic settings, complete verification is generally unavailable, while cheap checks can only falsify failures. articles.title: Augmented Hybrid TV Services. Habits, Preferences, Opinions and Expectations of Spanish Consumers
articles.summary: The convergence of hybrid broadcast and broadband delivery, companion devices, and immersive technologies enables new forms of interactive, personalized, and accessible TV services. This paper introduces the concept of Augmented Hybrid TV services and presents an exploratory user requirements and preliminary acceptance assessment for 5 representative use cases. articles.title: Synthesis Smuggling: Maliciously Hiding Inferred Personal Attributes in LLM Outputs
articles.summary: We propose Synthesis Smuggling, a novel threat model in which an adversarial LLM infers sensitive information about a user from routine assistance-seeking interactions and steganographically encodes that into innocuous-looking model-generated content. articles.title: A precision bound for gravitational transseries
articles.summary: We propose that the large $N$ transseries of a holographic observable above the black hole threshold admits a precision bound, a limit on how precisely the transseries can determine the observable at finite $N$, set by the data of its D-brane instanton sectors. articles.summary: We consider an individual-based model of niche construction built upon birth-death processes of d interacting biological entities (e.g., species, subpopulations or mutant strains in the same species) immersed in a slowly-varying environment which is influenced by the population state. articles.title: Twisting IKKT with branes
articles.summary: Motivated by the conjectural relationship between the IKKT matrix model and type IIB string theory, we classify supersymmetric twists of the matrix model, allowing for both dynamical and kinematical supercharges. articles.title: Observation of Genuine Multi-Time Quantum Memory
articles.summary: Memory effects in open quantum systems do not by themselves imply quantum memory, since non-Markovian dynamics can often be reproduced by classical-memory models. Known criteria certify the presence of quantum memory in the environment by comparing the evolution of the system at two different times. articles.title: LiveGeo: Benchmarking Geographic Agents in Continuously Evolving Worlds
articles.summary: We introduce GeoWorld, a controllable and continuously evolving geographic environment platform for LLM agents, and LiveGeo, a benchmark for evaluating reliable decision-making in real-world geographic environments using GeoWorld. articles.title: Global Fit Inference for LISA with samsara++
articles.summary: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) will observe a superposition of gravitational-wave signals, requiring joint inference of an unknown number of sources, parameters, and instrumental noise. To disentangle these contributions, that overlap in both time and frequency, a Global Fit (GF) analysis is needed. articles.title: Bayesian modeling of predictive stability under generalized Arrhenius non-linear kinetics
articles.summary: Predictive stability modeling is widely used in pharmaceutical development to establish product shelf-life by identifying the kinetic parameters that govern degradation behavior and using these parameters to extrapolate out in time. articles.title: Non-interferometric tests of gravitational decoherence models with mechanical oscillators
articles.summary: Phenomenological models of quantum-gravity-induced decoherence can leave observable effects even in experiments that do not rely on interferometric measurements. articles.title: Interactions from memory footprints: Cage-hopping, mnemotaxis & nonreciprocity
articles.summary: Cellular motility is integral to biological processes ranging from foraging to immune responses and cancer metastasis. While cells often navigate by sensing pre-existing environmental cues, many actively steer their future trajectories by remodeling their surroundings via shared, long-lived physicochemical trails called memory footprints. articles.title: Monopole catalysis with massive fermions: the fate of the twisted sector

articles.title: Noise-Adaptive Analog-Digital Preconditioning
articles.summary: Analog in-memory computing offers the potential to accelerate approximate inverse preconditioning, but hardware errors can degrade preconditioners designed in digital arithmetic. articles.title: Price-impact Martingale optimal transport
articles.summary: Martingale optimal transport (MOT) provides model-independent bounds for option prices calibrated to vanilla options, assuming frictionless trading in the underlying. articles.title: Programming Quantum Circuit Parameters with Large Language Models
articles.summary: Large language models (LLMs) have recently demonstrated the ability to generate parameters for variational quantum circuits without conventional optimization. However, the conditions under which this approach is effective remain unclear. articles.title: Characterising a population of fast-declining SNe Ia in galaxy cluster cores
articles.summary: Galaxy cluster cores, characterised by old stellar population and suppressed star-formation are ideal for studying the environmental dependence of Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia). articles.summary: Modern automated heuristic discovery (AHD) systems increasingly rival hand-crafted heuristics by leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs) to iteratively mutate and refine solutions. articles.title: Objects as Addresses: Instance Binding in Vision Transformer Attention
articles.summary: Humans naturally parse visual scenes into coherent individual objects rather than scattered features, a capability cognitive science calls object binding.
